canonical_encoding.frame_law: fields in SCHEMA ORDER (never sorted); str=u64len+utf8; int=8B LE signed; float=8B IEEE-754 bits (bit identity: -0.0 != 0.0, 1-ULP visible); bytes; bool; list=count+ordered frames, LIST ONLY (a tuple value is refused); field=namelen+name+value; ID=sha256(frame).hexdigest(); refusal contract: out-of-range ints raise struct.error and unframed types raise TypeError - every encoder refusal is an admission refusal, never a silent wrap
canonical_encoding.parent_embedding: child ids embed the parent digest as a hex str field, making composition order explicit

laws: cutoff equality is exact and typed; a trace produced at larger R is NEVER shared with a smaller R by filtering (b, seed gates, queue chronology and labels depend on R)
graph equivalence over real weights is not execution equivalence over ordered bits; the bits decide
changed graph flags/edge order/turns/obstacles/costs/profile/code cause identity misses even when many distances look unchanged
do not reverse a query or contract degree-two paths without a rounded-operation proof
a handle is not a durable cache identity; a pointer address is not a hash
trace representation: packed origin-major, indptr[O+1], destination_ids[nnz] int64, distance_bits[nnz] float64, immutable metadata; each slice strictly ascending ORIGINAL destination ids
store evaluated retained distance bits only; no rounded or compressed surrogates; no dense O*D or K*O*D intermediates; a consumer needing the full ODM keeps its original representation
one bounded producer tile at a time; measured trace bytes, packing, queues and leased memory; exceeding the trace budget selects recompute/streaming, never truncated-trace success
a partially computed trace carries incomplete status and can never be published as a cache hit
checked integer capacities and signed indices; representation proofs replace the prototype's typed-list narrowing warning, not warning suppression
validation: each trace slice vs actual full reference distances filtered in original index order; each job replay vs an independently executed full job
metric variation set varied individually: beta/plateau/midpoint/growth/KNN branch/coefficients/destination weights
identity tests must force different results for at least two cohort rows and validate all K jobs
exact-repeat control uses the current full-result cache
no invalid input becomes successful because an earlier trace hit avoided its validation

API surface (concept names adapt to existing backends, no parallel API): prepare_snapshot -> immutable GraphHandle; route(GraphHandle, query, dest) -> TraceHandle(capabilities, owner, bytes, complete); replay(TraceHandle, MetricPlan, weights) -> fresh ResultBundle; release(handle) after dependents complete
provenance_exclusion: provenance never enters any ID: two graphs with identical ordered bits share a GraphID regardless of where the bytes came from; a provenance-only difference never misses
